DRAFT for Moira to look over before posting

Yes, we're doing the tree again. Someone asked on here last week and it was lovely to be asked, so here is everything in one place.

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the shop window on Magdalen Street, and the lights go on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is doing her mince pies again. I'd come early if you want one. Last year they did not survive the first carol.

From Monday 16 November the memory tags will be in the shop. Write a name, or a few words, or whatever you like, and we'll hang it on the tree. We suggest a donation of £3 per tag. If you would rather write yours at home, there are envelopes on the counter to take with you, and you can bring it back when you're ready.

Every name on the tree is read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm in the day centre. You don't have to come to the service for your person's name to be read. You are very welcome if you'd like to, but it is no worse a remembrance for being done from your own armchair.

I want to say clearly that the tree is for anyone who is grieving. It isn't only for families the hospice has looked after. If you have lost someone anywhere, at any age, in any way, there is a place for them on it. And if you don't want to buy a tag, or write one, or say anything at all, please come and stand by the tree for a bit anyway. It's a warm shop, there is nobody who will ask you for anything, and the window is a good place to stand.

This will be seven years in November since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the counter with the same pen, and it has become one of the quieter parts of my year. I'm telling you only so you know that it does change a little, and that nobody in the shop will be surprised by whatever state you turn up in.

Thank you to everyone who came last year. 412 names went on the tree, and I can't tell you what it did for the shop to have that many people in it that evening, squeezed in the cold on the pavement and singing along badly. You made it feel like a street rather than a shop. We would love to see you again, and whoever you would like to bring with you.

See you on the 28th.

Jean
